segments.title: Barbarin's birth date and age; starting music at 14
segments.summary: He says he was born September 24, 1872, is 87, and took up music about age 14.

segments.title: First instrument alto; teacher Charles Sio of the French Opera
segments.summary: He began on alto; his teacher Charles Sio played in the French Opera band. The group struggles to identify the teacher's woodwind instrument.

segments.title: Playing with young bands; the Eureka band
segments.summary: He played with unnamed neighborhood bands as a learner, and names the Eureka band as the oldest colored band in town.

segments.title: Eureka band members and instrumentation
segments.summary: He names cornetist Oscar Giovanni and recalls six or seven young cornets, few trombones and many drummers, but few other names.

segments.title: Clarinets, saxophones and baritone horns in the early bands
segments.summary: Clarinetist Giovanni, E-flat and B-flat clarinets, no saxophones, and the difficult baritone part.

segments.title: Anthony Page, Vic Gaspar and the Excelsior Band
segments.summary: Questions on Anthony Page and Vic Gaspar, who played baritone and slide with the Excelsior Band; Barbarin was hired as an extra.

segments.title: Starting on cornet, put on alto horn by the professor Tio; later mellophone
segments.summary: The old professor judged the cornet too strong for him so he moved to alto horn, then mellophone.

segments.title: What early bands played and when ragtime dancing began
segments.summary: Concerts, parades, picnics, meter and quadrilles; ragtime dancing came long after the Spanish-American War.

segments.title: Family: Theresa Wilson, siblings and Two Row Street
segments.summary: Daughter Theresa Wilson gives her name and siblings; he had one sister and was born on Union Street near Royal.

segments.title: Band size, uniforms and dance music in the old brass bands
segments.summary: Twelve-man bands, blue and white uniforms, two drums at dances, waltz, mazurka and quadrille repertoire.

segments.title: Funeral music: slow marches, fast numbers and hymns
segments.summary: Slow marches to the cemetery, fast numbers after, hymns; he cannot recall tune titles.

segments.title: The Onward Brass Band and its early members
segments.summary: Asked about the Onward band, he names Bruno, Gabe Lawrence on tuba, and Henry.

segments.title: Band manager Steve Johnson, trombonist
segments.summary: The band's manager Steve Johnson played piston trombone; asked if he was related to Buddy Johnson.

segments.title: Theogene Baquet, his son George, and the Papa Tio clowning family
segments.summary: Excelsior leader Baquet who died in Texas, his son the clown, and Papa Tio and Lorenzo, who played with him.

segments.title: Manuel Perez leading his band; Eddie Jackson on tuba
segments.summary: Manuel Perez once led his band; pick-up bands had no fixed name; Eddie Jackson was a good tuba player.

segments.title: Piccolo players and absence of accordions
segments.summary: Piccolo players such as Doc Monique were few; accordions were not used.

segments.title: Hearing Buddy Bolden and the blues
segments.summary: He heard Bolden, whose players played by ear; everyone played the blues.

segments.title: The Pickwick Band and the Minatus brothers
segments.summary: The Pickwick Band's two Minatus brothers led it; they lived across the river. A brief return to the blues.

segments.title: Onward Band personnel: Perez, Gaspar, Johnson, Alexander, Matthews
segments.summary: The interviewer reads off a photo's lineup and Barbarin confirms who played, including Vic Gaspar, Buddy Johnson's brother and Adolph Alexander.

segments.title: Eddie Jackson and the Tuxedo band; Harrison Bond
segments.summary: Jackson played in the Tuxedo band with Barbarin; Harrison Bond filled in on trumpet when musicians were scarce.

segments.title: Joe Oliver leads the Onward band; Labor Day parade
segments.summary: Oliver took over the Onward band when Perez left for Chicago; the band played a colored Labor Day parade.

segments.title: Firemen's Day parades, carnival and Bastille Day
segments.summary: Playing the firemen's anniversary parade and banquet; no parades but picnics on July 14.

segments.title: Societies he played for and his church
segments.summary: Benevolent societies the band played for, and his Catholic church affiliation and baptism at St. Augustine.

segments.title: Dance halls: Mississippi Valley, Globe and Lek-E-Tay
segments.summary: He recalls playing for dances and Mardi Gras balls at several halls.

segments.title: Shot at a Mardi Gras ball
segments.summary: A fight broke out at a ball; he took a stray bullet and was hospitalized before Paul's birth.

segments.title: Calico balls, admission prices and dance band size
segments.summary: Calico balls, 25-cent admission, and ten-man bands usually without drums or piano.

segments.title: Diamond Brass Band and the minstrel show Ducongé
segments.summary: He knows nothing of the Diamond band; he knows Oscar Ducongé, who played anything.

segments.title: Economy Hall, Globe Hall and playing in the balcony
segments.summary: Economy Hall and Globe Hall balls; musicians played in the balcony.

segments.title: Fairground picnics and the bands that played them
segments.summary: Dance music for white or colored fairground and lakefront picnics; Robichaux, brass band and the Eagle band.

segments.title: Eagle Band, Frank Dusen, Celestin's Tuxedo band, Bill Jackson, Picou
segments.summary: Asked about members of various bands; he recalls Dusen, Celestin's Tuxedo band and Alphonse Picou.

segments.title: Henry Allen Sr. hiring him for brass bands
segments.summary: Mr. Allen always hired Barbarin for jobs, and they traded gigs.

segments.title: Sonny Henry, George Hooker, Creole and Claiborne Williams
segments.summary: Quick identifications of trumpeters and other players he knew.

segments.title: John Robichaux's orchestra and the Manetta band
segments.summary: Robichaux led a reading orchestra for white French Opera and balls; Manetta's band had the same instruments.

segments.title: Who was the best trumpet player; Perez and Oliver
segments.summary: Pressed to judge Perez against Joe Oliver, he declines and says both were good; session winds down.

segments.title: Alcibiade Jeanjacques, Punky Valentine and mixed neighborhoods
segments.summary: Good trumpeters, Punky Valentine's playing and house on Esplanade; whites and Creoles lived side by side.

segments.title: Batiste De Leo and musicians in the Spanish-American War
segments.summary: De Leo went to war on alto and switched to trombone; the interviewer's uncle Louis was a musician in 1898.
